claims.text: A refractory HEA in which tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum are replaced by vanadium, titanium, and chromium would be a promising plasma-facing-component material for fusion reactors.
Tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum are high-activation elements in the relevant fusion-neutron environment.
Vanadium, titanium, and chromium have lower neutron activation than tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum.
Replacing tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum with vanadium, titanium, and chromium would reduce the production of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
The proposed compositional substitution would significantly reduce long-term neutron-induced radioactivity.
The modified HEA would retain high-temperature mechanical strength comparable to tungsten-based counterparts.
The modified HEA would retain irradiation resistance comparable to tungsten-based counterparts.
The substituted alloy would form a robust BCC matrix.
The proposed BCC matrix would remain phase-stable under irradiation.
Maintaining a BCC matrix would preserve the alloy's high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance after substitution.
Conventional tungsten-rich refractory HEAs are currently used or investigated for high-temperature plasma-facing applications.
Conventional tungsten-rich refractory HEAs have good mechanical properties and irradiation resistance.
Conventional tungsten-rich refractory HEAs suffer from high neutron activation.
Fusion plasma-facing materials must operate at temperatures of at least approximately 1000 K for long durations.
Fusion divertor and plasma-facing materials experience severe particle and heat fluxes together with neutron-induced radiation damage.
Low activation is a required property for magnetic-fusion plasma-facing materials.
Tungsten is the leading or current elemental candidate for plasma-facing materials in tokamak fusion systems.
Tungsten is favored as a plasma-facing material because of its high melting temperature, low erosion rate, and low tritium retention.
The performance trade-offs of the modified alloy depend on balancing elemental substitution against phase stability.
The proposed substitutions may produce altered oxidation behavior or phase instability.
